title: Wearing the Shoes of Someone Who Passed Away

chapters.title: The Question of Wearing a Deceased Person's Shoes
chapters.about: Introduction to the question of what to do with the clothing and shoes of a niftar, referencing Sefer Hasidim.

chapters.title: Sefer Hasidim and Early Sources
chapters.about: Examining the statement in Sefer Hasidim by Rabbi Uda Hasid and practices mentioned in the books of Chesedek.

chapters.title: Rabbi Chaim Kanievsky's Remez from Devarim
chapters.about: Looking at a pasuk in Sefer Devarim regarding clothing in the plural versus shoes in the singular.

chapters.title: The Gemara in Masechet Hulina and Rationales
chapters.about: Connecting the topic to a Gemara in Masechet Hulina concerning animal hides and potential danger.

chapters.title: Rabbi Moshe Feinstein's View on Contagious Disease
chapters.about: Analyzing Rabbi Moshe Feinstein's explanation regarding potential contagious diseases and sanitizing items.

chapters.title: Dreams and Other Interpretations
chapters.about: Discussing a Gemara in Masechet Berakhot about dreams involving shoes and whether it serves as a rational basis for the halakha.

chapters.title: Leather Shoes, Slippers, and Conclusion
chapters.about: Distinguishing leather shoes from other footwear, and concluding on whether items can be given as sedaka.

summary: Rabbi Harari goes through the minhag and halakhot concerning whether a person can wear or give away the clothing and shoes of someone who passed away. He explores the source in Sefer Hasidim, the discussions among poskim including Rabbi Moshe Feinstein and Hacham Ovadia Yosef, and the practical applications regarding leather shoes, contagious illnesses, and giving items to sedakah.
questions: What should be done with the clothing and shoes of someone who passed away?
Does the prohibition in Sefer Hasidim apply to all shoes or only to leather shoes?
Can shoes of a niftar be given to sedaka or to family members?
What is the underlying reason behind the custom not to wear a deceased person's shoes?
Does the concern about a deceased person's shoes apply if they were not worn during a contagious illness?
